components.formal: Estimation relation: As the cost-sharing ratio increases, the likelihood of triggering correction also rises, which leads to a higher expected correction cost.
conditions: Under the C mechanism, if the correction cost satisfies l = 0 or l ≥ ɛ, imperfect cost audits have no impact on the optimal cost-sharing ratio, the expected client expense, or the system expense.
In such cases, regardless of the cost-sharing ratio γ, the contractor will either always correct audit outcomes that underestimate the true cost (when l = 0) or never correct them (when l ≥ ɛ).
The existence of audit noise ɛ, along with its distribution, is publicly known information and is independent of the contractor’s type, work rate, or realized cost.
